# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QH (Cave 1), Col. 10 | **Condition:** Better preserved

---

**10:1** What is flesh compared to this? And what is a creature of clay that it should do great wonders?

**10:2** And he is in iniquity from the womb, and in guilty unfaithfulness until old age.

**10:3** I know that righteousness belongs not to a mortal, nor perfection of way to a son of man.

**10:4** To God Most High belong all deeds of righteousness; and the way of man is not established.

**10:5** Except by the spirit that God has fashioned for him, to make perfect the way for the sons of man.

**10:6** That all His creatures may know the might of His power and the abundance of His mercies upon all the sons of His good-pleasure.

**10:7** As for me, trembling and terror have seized me, and all my bones are shattered.

**10:8** And my heart melts like wax before the fire, and my knees dissolve like water poured on a slope.

**10:9** For I have remembered my guilty deeds together with the unfaithfulness of my fathers.

**10:10** When the wicked rose against Your covenant and the vile against Your word.

**10:11** It is in iniquity from the womb, and in guilty unfaithfulness until old age.

**10:12** For I said, in my transgression I have been abandoned from Your covenant.

**10:13** But when I remembered the might of Your hand together with the abundance of Your mercies.

**10:14** Then I arose and stood, and my spirit was strengthened to stand against affliction.

**10:15** For I have leaned on Your covenant-faithfulness and the abundance of Your compassion.

**10:16** For You atone for iniquity, to purify man from guilt by Your righteousness.

**10:17** Not for the sake of man do You do this, but for the sake of Your glory.

**10:18** For You, You have created the righteous and the wicked.

**10:19** And who shall stand before You when Your judgment comes?

**10:20** And what is one born of woman that he should be accounted righteous?

**10:21** I know that righteousness belongs not to a mortal, nor perfection of way to a son of man.

**10:22** To God Most High belong all the deeds of righteousness, and the way of man is not established.

**10:23** Except by the spirit that God has fashioned for him.

**10:24** And You have formed all the works of the earth and the ordinance of all their labor from before eternity.

**10:25** And You have created the peoples for their service and a host of spirits for Your dominions.

**10:26** You have assigned their service for all the ages and the judgments of their appointed times.

**10:27** For You have established their decrees from before the ages, and the work of every [...] You have spread before You.

**10:28** The ways of man in all his works [...] You have spread before You.

**10:29** And it is known in the wisdom of Your knowledge that You have established their way from before eternity.

**10:30** And apart from You nothing is done. And nothing is known without Your will.

**10:31** To God Most High belong all deeds of righteousness; and the way of man is not established except by the spirit that God has fashioned for him.

**10:32** And You have fashioned the breath for the tongue, and You know its words.

**10:33** And You have established the fruit of the lips before they existed.

**10:34** And You set words on a measuring-line, and the utterance of the breath of the lips by measure.

**10:35** And You bring forth sounds according to their mysteries, and the outpourings of breath according to their reckoning.

**10:36** To make known Your glory and to recount Your wonders in all Your deeds of truth.

**10:37** And the judgments of Your righteousness and to praise Your name with the mouth of all who know You, and they shall bless You forever.

---

*EMET notes: Column 10 continues the anthropological meditation from Column 9. The repeated refrain "To God Most High belong all deeds of righteousness" (10:4, 10:22, 10:31) is a theological anchor. The remarkable section on speech and language (10:32-36) extends predestinarian theology to the very act of human utterance.*
